newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus says less interested in East Spar.
newsitem.headline: Novus says less interested in East Spar.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday that it was unlikely to make a bid for Mobil Corp's 35 percent stake in the East Spar gas field offshore Western Australia if it came on to the market.
Novus managing director Bob Williams said an earlier bid for WMC Ltd's 30 percent stake in the field, pre-empted by Santos Ltd, had been based on a combination of tax elements.
"We would at least take a look ... but I can't believe we would be very interested," he told Reuters. "There will be a lot of compteition and we feel we can do better deals elsewhere."

A report in the Sydney Morning Herald said Mobil unit Mobil Exploration and Producing Australia Pty Ltd was preparing to dispose of nearly A$400 million of assets inherited during its A$1.8 billion takeover of Ampolex Ltd last year.

The report identified the assets as a 25 percent interest in the Harriet oil and gas field, a 35 percent interest in the East Spar gas and condensate field and a 28.6 percent interest in the Macedon gas field, all offshore Western Australia.
A Mobil spokesman told Reuters the asset package to be sold had not yet been finalised.
Williams said Novus would have liked to enter East Spar in March, but had since made a US$26.5 million purchase in Oman and was pursuing other potential acquisitions outside Australia.
The company could spend about A$100 million, which would be debt funded, he added.
A spokesman for Santos, which lifted its stake in East Spar to 45 percent with the WMC purchse, declined to comment on whether it would look to boost its share in the field.
